references.text: The prophet Isaiah speaks of giving those who mourn in Zion oil of gladness instead of sorrow, a garment of praise instead of a spirit of despair. This points forward to the comfort that the mourning will receive, as Jesus mentions in Matthew 5:4.
The book of Psalms says that those who sow with tears shall reap with joy. This reflects the idea that those who mourn will find comfort and gladness, in line with the promise in Matthew 5:4.
In Ecclesiastes there is a time for everything, including a time to mourn and a time to dance, suggesting that sorrow will be replaced by joy, parallel to the comfort mentioned in Matthew 5:4.
In Luke's Gospel Jesus says that those who weep now shall laugh. This aligns with the promise of comfort to those who mourn in Matthew 5:4.

In Revelation there is a vision that God will wipe away every tear from their eyes, and there will be no more death or sorrow. This is the ultimate fulfillment of the promise of comfort to those who mourn that Jesus gives in Matthew 5:4.
